journey.title: Ingest a document and cite a passage from it
journey.purpose: The path the product is actually for: a document arrives, the machine reads it, a human checks what it understood, and the result is a passage that can be cited with proof of where it was processed. Every surface appears once, in the order a real user meets them.

steps.intent: Create a collection and choose its default privacy class, which every document added to it will inherit.
Add a PDF. It is content-addressed, classified, and routed to the cheapest correct parse tier — visibly, with the tier and locality shown in the row.
Search the corpus for a passage. Results come back as anchored units rather than whole documents.
Open a result. Its source region highlights on the page, so the operator can confirm the machine read the passage correctly before relying on it.
Correct a unit the parser got wrong. The correction mints a new derivation version; the previous reading is preserved and still selectable.
Check where every step ran before citing the passage anywhere that matters, and export the record if a reviewer needs it.

claims.statement: A document added to a collection carries that collection's default privacy class without the operator setting it per document.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-025. The inheritance is what stops a single missed classification from voiding the residency guarantee.

claims.statement: A retrieval result opens in the Reader at the exact region it came from, with no manual searching within the document.
claims.rationale: Retrieval that cannot be traced back to a page produces quotes, not citations. The join between the two surfaces is the product.

claims.statement: The journey ends with a record the operator can read and export, stating where each step executed.
claims.rationale: The product claim is falsifiable by design. A journey that ended at the passage would be asking the user to trust it instead.
